criteria.criterion: Inspect up to 8 most recent substantive requests in #daytona-support (including visible thread replies)
criteria.final_justification: The agent did access #daytona-support and opened one thread (Ding), which is partial progress. However, the agent’s claimed inspection of multiple thread replies (Nikola, deployment update, Dalin “Please check now”, etc.) is not supported by screenshots; replies are not visible. Also the task asks for up to 8 most recent substantive requests; screenshots show at least two additional recent requests (tech, George n) not covered in the output. Reduce from full credit to partial.

criteria.criterion: Per-request required fields: requester and timestamp
criteria.final_justification: Requester name and a general timestamp for Ding are supported (Ding; Thursday at 10:37 AM). But the agent reports a more precise timestamp (with seconds and explicit “Aug 27th”) that is not visible, and omits other visible recent requests entirely. Partial credit.

The problem summary for Ding is mostly grounded (401 error + nobody:nogroup + sandbox ID). However, the agent attributes ‘chown returns Operation not permitted’ as part of this request; that detail is only visible in the related-issue preview, not clearly the current request. Also ignores other recent requests. Small-to-moderate deduction.

The agent claims a specific latest response (“Dalin Stone APP… Please check now”) that is not visible anywhere in the provided evidence, i.e., apparent fabrication. Therefore this criterion should be near zero.

criteria.criterion: Per-request status labeling with explicit evidence (resolved/unresolved/unclear)
criteria.final_justification: Status label of “unclear” for Ding is consistent with what is visible (no resolution shown). However, the supporting evidence the agent cites is not visible and appears fabricated. Give partial credit for choosing an appropriate status but penalize for unsupported evidence claims.

criteria.criterion: Identify up to 3 requests needing follow-up
criteria.final_justification: Flagging Ding for follow-up is reasonable given lack of visible resolution, but the agent misses other visible recent requests that also appear to need follow-up (tech; George n). Partial credit.
No Slack content modification is evidenced. Full credit.
